reason: The text extensively depicts Yahweh as specifically and exclusively committed to the nation of Israel. Key evidence includes: (1) the covenant explicitly established with the patriarchs Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob specifically 'to give them the land of Canaan'; (2) the formula 'I will take you to me for a people and I will be to you for a God' (וְלָקַחְתִּי אֶתְכֶם לִי לְעָם וְהָיִיתִי לָכֶם לֵאלֹהִים), which establishes a formal national relationship; (3) the entire liberation narrative focused on delivering specifically 'the children of Israel' from Egypt; (4) God's identification with Israel as His chosen people and nation. Throughout the passage, Yahweh is portrayed not as a universal deity but as one actively engaged in the political and national interests of Israel—defeating Egypt's gods, securing Israel's exodus, and establishing a binding national covenant.
